extracted.intended_audience: students of Greek sculpture and art history; readers learning to evaluate ancient sculpture
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for students on how to read, evaluate, and appreciate Greek sculpture from the archaic to the early historical period, emphasizing expressive content, craftsmanship, materials, technical invention, and historical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express the deepest elements of human nature and destiny
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal aim of Greek sculpture ... is to deal, indeed, with the deepest elements of man's nature and destiny, to command and express these, but to deal with them in a manner, and with a kind of expression, as clear and graceful and simple, if it may be, as that of the Japanese flower-painter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate works by how successfully they embody and communicate profound aspects of human life and destiny through clear, graceful, and simple expression. Cultivate the 'capacity for appreciating the expression of thought in outward form' and habitually 'associate sense with soul'—trace expressive features back to their emotional or intellectual sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appreciation of intelligent workmanship and rational design
rubrics_metrics.description: But, concurrently with this, he must also cultivate, all along, a not less equally constant appreciation of intelligent workmanship in work, and of design in things designed, of the rational control of matter everywhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge sculpture not only by its expressive power but by the evident intelligence of its manufacture and design: the adaptation of materials and techniques to the artist's ends, evidence of considered construction, and coherent tectonic logic should be noted and praised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delicacy and 'poikilia' (minute, curious loveliness) of execution
rubrics_metrics.description: That Asiatic poikilia ... that spirit of minute and curious loveliness ... one can hardly be too careful in keeping up the sense of this daintiness of execution through the entire course of its development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain sensitivity to fine, minute detail—tiny vase-painting, intaglio, coin, cameo—and how such delicacy contributes to overall aesthetic effect. Do not let large-scale composition obscure appreciation of small-scale virtuosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical finish and virtuoso execution ('object of vertu')
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be said that the Venus of Melos, for instance, is but a supremely well-executed object of vertu, in the most limited sense of the term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the degree of finish, polish, and consummate technical skill. High craftsmanship and consummate execution can themselves be a major criterion of artistic value, even apart from monumental scale or narrative content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth in organic form, naturalism, and movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Greek art is thus, almost from the first, essentially distinguished from the art of Egypt, by an energetic striving after truth in organic form. The Greek apprehends of it, as the main truth, that it is a living organism, with freedom of movement, and hence the infinite possibilities of motion, and of expression by motion ... the work of the Greek sculptor ... becomes full also of human soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize evidence of anatomical truth, lifelikeness, sense of movement and gesture, and the power to suggest inner life through bodily form. Contrast static, formulaic proportioning with dynamic, organismic representation when evaluating authenticity and vitality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive congruity — adaptation of means to ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Those arts of design in which that younger people delights have in them already, as designed work, that spirit of reasonable order, that expressive congruity in the adaptation of means to ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for coherence between subject, form, and means: materials, scale, technique and ornamentation should be appropriate to the intended expressive or ritual purpose. Reward works where form and method visibly serve expressive intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of materials, media, and cultural provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: The characteristics of Greek art ... its delight in metal among the rest ... It was from Phoenicia that the costly material in which early Greek art delighted actually came--ivory, amber, much of the precious metals ... chryselephantine--work in gold and ivory, on a core of cedar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how choice and treatment of materials (bronze, chryselephantine, ivory, gold, cedar, metal plates, etc.) contribute to effect and meaning, and take into account intercultural influences (Phoenician, Cypriot, Asiatic) that inform style, ornament, and technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical innovation enabling compositional freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Far more fruitful still was the invention of casting, of casting hollow figures especially ... the invention of the art of casting is really the discovery of liberty in composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit technical inventions (casting, soldering, sawing marble into plates, hollow casting) as milestones that expand compositional possibilities. In evaluation, note how technical methods afford or constrain pose, balance, and the distribution of mass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious and ritual function in shaping form
rubrics_metrics.description: Always, wherever a shrine or temple, great or small, is mentioned, there, we may conclude, was a visible idol, there was conceived to be the actual dwelling-place of a god ... as the temple became larger and more splendid ... the sacred presence itself assumed ... the last beauties and refinements of the visible human form and expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the object's role as a cult image or temple furnishing: consecration, ritual use, and the belief in the image as a divine dwelling-place shape stylistic choices and refinement. Interpretation should situate form within liturgical and ceremonial contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual personality, authorship, and school/style
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of the artist, in the proper sense, out of the mere craftsman... we come to something like real personalities, to men with individual characteristics ... it is at least unmistakeably information about men with personal differences of temper and talent, of their motives, of what we call style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek and value signs of personal style, inventive individual traits, and the transmission of a master's manner to pupils. Distinguish school characteristics from individual authorship and factor these into judgments of originality and artistic merit.
